Hi! I created a PR for the first proper result building on top of multi tape Turing machines, a bound on the number of reachable configurations in bounded space and the subsequent results L in P and PSPACE in EXP.
The proofs are clean but I wonder 1) if some of the machinery already exists in LTS and 2) if the proofs about growth rate estimations can somehow be simplified

About 2: I had a look at the growth rate pr (https://github.com/leanprover/cslib/pull/468 ) but it looks like it has the same problems or at least I didn’t find anything. I started an ai process to check if it can find a better formalism, let’s see.
Following the recommendation by @Samuel Schlesinger I split the PR into smaller parts. The first split out is PR 768

About 1) at one point I have a „manual“ proof of the fact that if two configurations repeat in the computation, then the TM does not halt. Essentially, this is a property of iterated functions / dynamical systems: the step function has a fixed point (periodic point with period 1) at the halting configuration and if there is another periodic point in the orbit reachable from the initial configuration, then the halting configuration is not reachable.
The question is: should we prove this using the machinery of iterated functions or would a „manual“ proof be better?
